name: mopop-kit
summary:
parts/forms.mjs rewritten: each colour is now a low body (coloured walls, flat, gently curved grey polished_andesite roof) with 2-4 tall curved 1-2-thick SHEETS rising from the ground along arcs of its wall, each peeling over at the top in a curled lip that overhangs the side it rolls toward. Heights range from purple 44 and blue 39 down to red/gold/magenta 22-32 and silver B 22.
Sheets end in gaps with dark tinted-glass slots. Grey creases mark where two colours meet, and a later mass tucks behind an earlier one. Disconnected sheet bits are dropped (0 floating), and sea lanterns are set into the roofs.
Footprint, monorail, train, lobbies, floors, plaza, colours and seam courses are unchanged. build.nbt saved and walkable; v2.nbt kept.

revisions.comment:
Owner's comment on the Seattle Center render: the surrounding buildings look rough. For MoPOP specifically, fix these (keep the footprint, the plot, the monorail street and train, and 1.21.1 blocks):

1. The forms read as separate hemisphere domes sitting side by side. Gehry's MoPOP is a few continuous, billowing sheet-metal masses that lean, overhang and fold into one another. Merge neighbouring lobes so they flow together with creases where they meet; give each mass a leaning, asymmetric profile (taller on one side, rolling over at the top like a wave or a crumpled sheet), and let some overhang the walkways below. No hemisphere caps.
2. The purple mass is a vertical-striped cylinder with a flat pink roof. Make it a curved, leaning, crumpled purple form whose top rolls over into a rounded crown: no flat roof slab, no pink rim, no straight vertical drum walls.
3. The surfaces are speckled with randomly scattered blocks. Clad each mass as shingled metal: one main block per colour with a close second tone laid in regular horizontal seam courses (for example purple concrete with purple terracotta courses; yellow concrete with gold-block seams; light grey concrete with iron-block seams for the silver; red concrete with red terracotta; light blue concrete with cyan terracotta). No random dithering.
4. Keep the strong colours (purple, gold, silver, red, blue). The silver masses should read silver-bright, not white.
revisions.summary: The forms are now leaning, merged masses with rolled-over crowns and regular seam courses; the last renders show the purple, gold and blue reading clearly as waves. A new parts/forms.mjs replaces the domes: all eight masses (purple, silver A, hood, blue, bridge, red, gold, magenta, silver B) are one shape, built from the regenerated build.nbt (v1.nbt kept). Where two colours meet there is no wall between them, just a crease line. Stairs, slabs and the random speckle are gone from the shells. The footprint, monorail street, train, lobbies, doors and grounds are unchanged; floors are now trimmed to stay inside the new walls. Check: walkable, 0 floating blocks, 1 stray block (a single yellow block sticking out of gold at 24,23,85). Some masses still read as rounded humps from the iso views.
applied: 1. Forms flow together: overlapping masses merge into one shape with no wall between them, and a gray_concrete crease runs where two colours meet. Each mass leans toward its tall side (tilted crown, low side about 45-60% of the high side). Its crown rolls over like a wave, the wall bulges at the shoulder, and two diagonal folds are cut into each mass. The masses overhang the glass lobbies and the entrance landing (purple over the east street lobby, red over the west lobby, the hood over the main doors). No hemisphere caps.

The blue bridge lobe was a flat-topped cylinder; it is now a blue form that starts at the y18 soffit over the track and runs into the blue body. The glass strip over the train and the north/south gallery glass bands are cut into it.

2. Purple: a leaning, crumpled form, tall at the north-west (y44), rolling over toward the monorail street and falling to the south-east. It has a rounded crown and fold grooves. The flat purpur roof, the pink rim, the vertical walls and the magenta streaks are gone; the slot window is cut into the leaning north face.

3. Cladding: one main block per colour, with a second tone every 4th row on the walls: purple concrete / purple terracotta, yellow concrete / gold block, red concrete / red terracotta, light blue concrete / cyan terracotta, magenta concrete / magenta terracotta. Silver is light grey concrete with iron-block courses every 3rd row. The other crowns are plain main block, so they don't show bullseye rings. No random dithering, and no white quartz or diorite stair speckle.

4. The strong colours are kept. Silver uses the light grey concrete and iron courses on its crown too, so it reads bright metal: iron_block as the main block read white, and plain grey concrete read dull.

Kept working: all doors D1-D7 are open (lobby boxes and D7's cells stay clear of the forms), nothing from the forms is in the monorail corridor, the height stays under y46, and walkable end to end is true. The palette's outlier flags for the seam blocks are the courses you asked for.
skipped: The metal skins are full blocks, with no stairs or slabs. Same-colour stairs don't exist for concrete, and the off-tone stairs (quartz, diorite, purpur) were what caused the speckle and the pink rim. The curves come from the shape itself.
From the iso views some masses (magenta, the south silver) still read as rounded humps more than crumpled sheets. Sharper creases or more fold geometry would be the next step if wanted.
The fin, monorail, train, lobbies, plaza and grounds are left as they were (not mentioned in the comment).

revisions.comment:
Owner's comment on the render: "what's with those hemispheres in the foreground?" v2 turned the domes into rounded egg/jelly-bean blobs; from the air they still read as inflated balloons, not Gehry. Fix the FORM (keep footprint, plot, monorail street and train, colours, the seam-course cladding, 1.21.1 blocks):

1. Gehry's MoPOP is made of SHEETS, not inflated volumes. Build each colour as a tall curved wall (a shell 1-2 blocks thick) that rises from the ground and peels over at the top like a breaking wave or a curled sheet of metal, with its top edge overhanging the side it curls toward. No rounded caps, no egg tops, no closed ellipsoids.
2. Where two sheets meet, make a sharp crease or a ridge line, and let one sheet tuck behind or overlap the next; leave gaps and slots between sheets (glass or dark recesses in the gaps) so the composition reads as several folded pieces, not one lump.
3. Vary the heights strongly: the purple/blue mass is the tallest, nearly vertical on its outer face and folding inward at the top; the gold and red pieces are lower and lean outward; the silver piece is a crumpled cluster with sharp ridges by the monorail.
4. Roofs between and behind the sheets are lower, flat or gently curved in grey, so the colourful sheets stand proud of them (from the air you should see the sheet edges as lines, not blobs).
Look at the photos in ../sf-landmarks/refs/seattle-center/mopop/ and the concept image before building.

applied: 1. Sheets, not volumes: the egg/ellipsoid crowns are gone. Each colour stands as tall curved sheet arcs (1-2 blocks thick) that rise from the ground on its wall line. At the top each sheet rolls through a quarter-to-half circle into a lip that overhangs inward (purple, blue, east silver, south-west magenta) or outward (gold, red, hood, magenta east). Under the sheets is a low enclosed body for the floors.

2. Creases and gaps: separate sheet arcs with gaps between them, their tops falling into the roof at both ends. A dark tinted_glass slot runs down the wall where each sheet ends. A gray_concrete crease line marks where two colours touch. Later masses tuck behind earlier ones, so sheets overlap instead of merging into one lump.

3. Heights varied strongly: purple's sheet reaches 44 (nearly vertical outer face, folding inward over its roof) and blue's 39. Gold (32), red (28) and magenta (26) are lower and lean outward 2-3 blocks with outward lips; an outward lip that would leave the plot outline or cross the street stands straight and curls inward instead. Silver A's east side by the monorail is a crumpled cluster of sheets with zig-zag sharp ridges (silver hood and silver B ridged too).

4. Low grey roofs: every body is capped by a flat, gently curved polished_andesite roof well below its sheets (bodies from y 14 to y 30), so the coloured sheet edges stand proud as lines from the air. Sea lanterns are set into the roofs on a 9-block grid.
skipped: The red form's outward-leaning west sheet mostly turns inward where its lip would leave the plot outline, so from the west the red still reads largely as a flat-topped block with little lip showing.
The blue bridge over the monorail gets no sheet of its own (it keeps its grey roof at y30 with the blue body's sheets beside it), so its soffit glass strip and gallery windows stay where they were.

Interior light at ground level is still dark (12,386 of 13,540 floor cells at light 0, the same as v2). Lighting wasn't in this comment, so it is untouched, but the building does not yet meet the brief's no-mob-spawn rule.
The check flags 48 roof sea lanterns as 'unsupported': they are full blocks set into the roof over hollow rooms, not hanging lights, so I left them.
Not mentioned, so left as they were: footprint, monorail beams/pylons/train, lobbies, doors, floors and stairs, plaza and grounds, colours, seam-course cladding.
